card.title: Status of flora in Nepal and world representation

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Nepal holds roughly 2–3% of the world's flowering plants on 0.1% of its land — about 7,000 angiosperms, 500–600 ferns, 1,100+ bryophytes and 30+ gymnosperms, many endemic to the Himalaya. The reasons are the country's enormous altitudinal range (60 m to 8,848 m), its position at the junction of the Palaearctic and Indo-Malayan realms, the monsoon climate and complex topography.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
The timberline, near 4000 m, is where trees stop. The snowline is higher. Alpine herbs live between them, so a sentence that puts Sal above the timberline has left the tropical belt.
Chir pine, Pinus roxburghii, marks the subtropical hills. Blue pine is a cooler-belt tree. Community forestry is the management story of the middle hills, not a type of vegetation.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Endemic vs endangered:** endemic = geographically restricted to one region; endangered = at high risk of extinction. A species can be endemic and common, or widespread and endangered.  ·  **Flora vs vegetation:** flora is the list of plant species; vegetation is the actual plant cover communities (forest, grassland) on the ground.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m):** Define flora. **Answer.** The **complete plant life of a given region or period** — the species list itself — as distinct from **vegetation**, which is the actual standing plant cover those species build.  ·  **Short answer (2m):** What is a biodiversity hotspot? **Answer.** A region with **exceptionally high endemism that is under severe threat of habitat loss** (≥70% habitat already gone). The **Himalaya** is one of the world's 36 hotspots, which puts Nepal's flora among the planet's conservation priorities.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Altitude is Nepal's latitude** — vertical zonation compresses what continents spread over thousands of kilometres.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Nepal: ~0.1% of world land but ~2–3% of world flowering plants (~6,000–7,000 species); ~500–600 ferns, ~1,100+ bryophytes, ~30+ gymnosperms.  ·  Four reasons for richness: altitudinal range (60 m → 8,848 m), two-realm junction (Palaearctic + Indo-Malayan), monsoon climate, complex topography/microclimates.  ·  Vegetation zones by altitude: subtropical (Sal) → lower temperate (pine) → upper temperate (oak–rhododendron) → subalpine (birch–fir) → alpine (grasses) → nival (lichens).  ·  Himalaya = one of the world's 36 biodiversity hotspots; many endemic flowering plants.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Rhododendron arboreum (lali gurans) is Nepal's national flower; rhododendron forests peak between 1,800 and 3,600 m.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: ***Betula utilis*** (bhojpatra) — subalpine birch whose bark was used as paper.
